wcs_p1r_thinking: Say you've been at something for weeks and not much is changing. I think part of you might be hoping someone will just tell you to quit, and part of you might be scared to. Before either, I'd check whether you actually did the part you meant to practice, or mostly read about it and got ready to (reading this counts as getting ready). And if it was comforting your little one, was the loving grown-up really there? Your little one would notice if it wasn't, the way you notice a hug from someone who's checking their phone. I'd borrow that grown-up first, then come back to your little one.
wcs_p2r_thinking: How many tries is enough? I really don't know, and I'd be suspicious of anyone who gives you a number, since some things shift in a day and some take about as long as learning guitar. If it's making things worse, or you just can't do it right now, I'd change course sooner. Not wanting to do it anymore can count too, but I'd hear that no out first, sudden or not, since it might be a part of you that's trying to protect you. And if what it said would happen keeps not happening when you're doing it right, I think you've learned something real about it. A clearly better-supported way is worth switching for too.
